title: preflight-hardware-quirks-and-terraform-adapters-playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note gathers hardware-quirk observations, recommended terraform adapter patterns, and a conservative cluster bootstrap + upgrade sequence for on-prem K8s deployments (both bare metal and vSphere-backed metal). Intended as a pragmatic checklist for field engineers and infra owners during first-run installs and fragile upgrades.

Status/context:
- Draft: based on three field installs (Q2–Q3 2024) and post-mortem from a failed upgrade in staging.
- Audience: SEs, SREs, Solutions Eng, and Terraform authors.
- Goals: reduce first-boot failures, shorten mean-time-to-healthy, and limit blast radius during control plane changes.

High-level constraints we assume:
- Sites vary: room for 10–200 nodes.
- Some sites have vSphere (VMs backed by SAN/NAS), others are fully bare-metal with IPMI/BMCs.
- Network trust: management plane often isolated; some air-gapped installs exist.
- Customers expect replacable nodes but not necessarily identical hardware revisions.

Observed hardware quirks (field notes):
1) NIC offload and checksum issues
   - Symptoms: kubelet/node readiness oscillates with high packet loss during constant RPCs (etcd/health checks).
   - Root cause: older Broadcom NICs with broken GRO/TSO handling in vendor drivers.
   - Mitigation: preflight script disables offloads (ethtool -K <iface> tx off rx off tso off gso off) in OS provisioning stage. Add as a configurable hook in the terraform module.

2) RAID controller timeouts during OS install
   - Symptoms: intermittent installer hangs, kernel reporting controller timeouts, time-skewed system clocks.
   - Mitigation: ensure RAID firmware >= vendor-min (callout in preflight). Use vendor CLI to set queue_depth conservative value, or prefer passthrough if possible. Document fallback: install to local NVMe if controller unreliable.

3) BMC/IPMI firmware health and dual-NIC oddities
   - Symptoms: walks where BMC reboots mid-provision. Some BMCs map management NICs to different MACs after firmware update.
   - Mitigation: validate BMC firmware and snapshot MAC addresses in inventory. Add explicit BMC reboot tolerance window in automation (retry with exponential backoff, do not reassign IP until stable).

4) Boot order flakiness with combined iPXE+UEFI stacks
   - Symptoms: first reboot falls back to local disk, block-until-boot causes provisioning to terminate.
   - Mitigation: explicit UEFI NVRAM variable set via vendor tools or ipmitool/chassis bootdev pxe options. Add 2nd-check: verify next-boot state immediately after provisioning step.

Recommended Terraform module adapter patterns
- Goal: terraform modules should be declarative about hardware intent ("provision 3 control-plane nodes with BMC, NIC-quirks hook, and local disk policy"), and expose small, composable hooks for provider-specific quirks.

1) module interface sketch (input vars):
   - control_plane_count (int)
   - worker_count (int)
   - bmc_inventory_id (string)
   - nic_profile (string) -- values: default | disable-offloads | force-multi-queue
   - boot_policy (string) -- values: ipxe | uefi-pxe | cd-rom
   - provision_hooks (list) -- ordered list of shell snippets to run (bootstrap time)
   - idempotency_token (string) -- ensure re-run safety 

2) outputs and state considerations:
   - machine_asset_ids (list)
   - last_provision_state (string)
   - caution: avoid embedding ephemeral credentials in state; instead store only references to vault/KMS objects.

3) Hook pattern implementation notes:
   - Hooks are stored as configmap-like blobs in a provisioning artifact bucket or local file server. Terraform writes only pointer and checksum to state. Provisioners fetch and exec.
   - Provide dry-run mode that echoes hook commands in logs instead of executing (useful for airgapped validation).

Cluster bootstrap sequence (conservative, repeatable):
Precondition: inventory validated (BMC up, NICs mapped, firmware OK), NTP reachable or pre-seeded time, and required secrets provisioned to secrets manager.

1) Provision nodes to OS image with a clean partitioning scheme name (e.g., redwood-k8s-boot).
2) Run node-level preflight hooks: disable NIC offloads (if nic_profile != default), ensure kernel modules for vendor drivers present, write ssh host key fingerprint to inventory.
3) Ensure control-plane nodes have persistent storage for etcd: prefer local NVMe RAID-1 or SAN LUNs with correct multipath config.
4) Init first control-plane with explicit CA (do not rely on automatic self-signed per Kubeadm unless for PoC). Store CA and certs into customer KMS where possible.
5) Join second and third control-plane nodes sequentially, verifying etcd quorum and health after each join (etcdctl endpoint status; kubectl get componentstatuses).
6) Wait until core control-plane metrics meet SLO: api-server REST latency < 200ms 95th and etcd leader under acceptable latency.

Upgrade playbook (control-plane focused, conservative approach):
- Principle: minimize simultaneous control-plane changes; always keep quorum >= majority.

1) Pre-upgrade validation
   - Collect current versions and binary checksums.
   - Run smoke suite: scheduler scheduling test, kube-dns resolution, core api latency.
   - Snapshot etcd (etcdctl snapshot save). Verify restore in a sandbox before proceeding.

2) Canaries
   - Upgrade single control-plane node (non-leader preferred). Validate 10–15 minute steady state. If CPU/IO spikes or elevated latency, rollback.

3) Full control-plane rotation
   - Upgrade remaining control-plane nodes one at a time. For each node: cordon -> drain with appropriate grace period -> upgrade binaries -> restart services -> verify local etcd membership and API health -> uncordon.

4) Worker pool upgrades
   - For each worker pool: maintain maxUnavailable = 1 or as low as tolerable; prefer rolling upgrades by draining nodes and replacing them via terraform apply to avoid in-place binary changes.

5) Post-upgrade verification
   - Run e2e smoke tests, validate latency histograms, and run a perf-regression check using a small traffic replay.

Data plane/Storage considerations during upgrades:
- For local PVs: implement node-level evacuation strategy and prefer move to PVC backed by external storage if possible.
- For CSI drivers with older versions, ensure reconciliation loops won't re-provision volumes during object format changes. Test in staging with volume-heavy workloads.

Idempotency and error handling patterns for automation
- Use task state markers on the node (e.g., /var/lib/redwood/provisioned: checksum) to prevent re-execution of destructive tasks.
- Make every step retryable and limit side-effects until the final commit step (two-phase commit pattern).
- Record all provisioner stdout/stderr artifacts to central object store for postmortem.

Troubleshooting quick cheatsheet (what to check first):
- Node unreachable after provision: check BMC log, provisioning server reachability, DHCP lease assigned, next-boot NVRAM value.
- Kubelet flapping: check dmesg for NIC errors, run ethtool -S, look for register overflow.
- etcd follower consistently behind: inspect disk latencies, check fsync behavior, and verify multipath config.

Unresolved questions / follow-ups
- Do we standardize on external CA for all customers, or provide a policy decision matrix? (PD decision needed)
- Should terraform modules expose a complete "provisioning dry-run" that can be executed in airgapped sites without network egress?
- Add automated firmware validator that can reconcile firmware to a declared baseline? (worth an RFC)

Action items (short-term):
- [ ] Patch terraform module to expose nic_profile and provision_hooks (owner: Marcus Chen, due: 2024-10-15)
- [ ] Add an offline dry-run validator that runs in local VM lab (owner: Elena Park, due: 2024-11-01)
- [ ] Draft customer-facing one-pager on preflight requirements and expectations (owner: Asha Patel, due: 2024-10-07)

Appendix: useful commands (field kit)
- Check NIC stats: ethtool -S eth0 | egrep "(tx_|rx_).*errors"
- Disable offloads: sudo ethtool -K eth0 tx off rx off tso off gso off gro off
- Force next-boot to PXE (ipmitool): ipmitool chassis bootdev pxe options=single
- Walk etcd health: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://<ep>:2379 --cacert=ca.pem --cert=client.pem --key=client-key.pem endpoint health
- Snapshot etcd: etcdctl snap save /tmp/etcd-$(date +%s).db

Notes to self and comms style:
- Keep checklist short for field runbook; move large diagnostics to a separate diagnostics playbook that can be invoked by ticket.
- Prefer explicit examples over abstract guidance when writing customer-facing steps.

End of draft.
